ai.title: Referral POST auth switched to sessionToken lookup
ai.summary: web/src/app/api/referrals/route.ts POST handler replaces getServerSession with direct database query. Request body validated via zod for referralCode and authToken. Auth flow now resolves userId by matching sessionToken column against provided authToken. Eliminates NextAuth session dependency for this specific endpoint.

eli5.text: The referral redemption system now checks your identity using your login token directly against the database instead of going through the main authentication service. When you submit a referral code along with your token, the system finds your account by matching the token to verify you're allowed to claim the referral. This change lets the referral feature work even if the primary login system is temporarily unavailable. You'll notice nothing different in your experience, except the referral process may work more reliably during authentication outages.

ai.title: Add timeout to parallel patch generation
ai.summary: generateBestOfNPatch now dynamically times out parallel patch generation. Mechanism: Promise.race waits for first patch, sets timeout to 1.75x duration plus 2s, then Promise.all filters nulls. Scope: backend/src/generate-patch.ts only. Detail: comparePrompt and bestPatchNumber validation updated to handle variable patch counts.

eli5.text: The background code that creates alternative versions of code changes before they are applied now stops itself from running too long. It watches the first finished attempt, uses that speed to set a deadline for the other attempts, and gives up on any that are still waiting when that deadline passes. You will not see this while using the product, since it only affects how the system prepares code suggestions behind the scenes. This only applies to the internal process that generates these code alternatives, so it does not change how anything else works.

ai.title: Clarify referral bonus and usage limit copy
ai.summary: Referral copy now specifies bidirectional credit rewards (`CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS` per month for both referrer and referee). `showUsageWarning` in `npm-app/src/client.ts` displays exact usage counts (`${usage}/${limit}` credits) and shifts upgrade/referral prompts from yellow to green. `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx` and `npm-app/src/menu.ts` updated to match the 'both earn' phrasing.

eli5.text: The wording that appears when you run low on coding credits and when others sign up through your referral link was rewritten to be clearer and friendlier. The usage notice now tells you the exact number of credits left (for example "120/200 credits used") instead of just a general warning, and the text encouraging you to upgrade your account or ask friends to join is shown in green instead of yellow. The referral message everywhere you see it now says that both you and the person you refer get the bonus credits each month, removing any doubt about who earns the reward. No access, limits, or the actual number of bonus credits changed; only the text and color of the messages did.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.92
ai.summary: Incremented package version to 1.0.92 in npm-app/package.json. No functional code changes included in this commit.

eli5.text: The app's version label was bumped to 1.0.92, which bundles in a few user-noticeable tweaks: referral links now require an active login session, parallel patch generation will time out instead of hanging, and the referral bonus text now clarifies that both the referrer and referee get monthly credit. These changes are live today for anyone using the referral feature or generating patches.

ai.title: System prompt: enforce latest package versions
ai.summary: Updated system prompt to explicitly instruct agent to use install commands (e.g. `npm install`) instead of guessing versions in `package.json`. Added warning to ensure latest versions are fetched across all package managers (Maven, etc.). Changes affect `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: The instructions given to the internal assistant have been updated to emphasize using proper installation commands (like npm install, and equivalents in other package managers such as Maven) instead of manually guessing and writing version numbers into configuration files. The assistant will now be more careful to ensure the latest versions of packages are fetched, regardless of the programming language or package manager being used.
